sources.entry: bittorrent-tracker - Simple, robust, BitTorrent tracker (client and server) implementation. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: A Node.js implementation of a BitTorrent tracker, including both client and server code, supporting HTTP, UDP, and WebTorrent tracker types.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a BitTorrent tracker server that accepts announce and scrape requests over HTTP, UDP (BEP 15), and WebSocket (WebTorrent trackers), and returns peer lists to clients. It also provides a client API that connects to trackers, sends announce/scrape requests, and emits peer and update events. The server can be configured to enable or disable each protocol, expose tracker statistics at /stats and /stats.json, and use a filter function to allow or block torrents by info hash, peer ID, or secret key. Supports IPv4 and IPv6, and optional trust of x-forwarded-for headers behind a reverse proxy. It can be run as a library or through a global command-line tool with port and interval options.
use_cases: host a tracker for WebTorrent swarms
scrape seeder and leecher counts from trackers
whitelist or blacklist torrents on a tracker
connect a Node.js app to BitTorrent trackers
notable: Includes both tracker server and tracker client in one module
Supports HTTP, UDP (BEP 15), and WebTorrent (WebSocket) tracker types
Server filter callback can allow or deny torrents using async checks on info hash and request parameters
Built-in web statistics page at /stats and JSON at /stats.json
Used by WebTorrent, peerflix, and playback according to the README
caveats: WebTorrent tracker protocol is described as 'BEP forthcoming', so it is not yet a standard BEP
Client proxy support differs by transport and Node version (undici Agent on Node 16+, http.Agent before)
Requires Node.js and npm; the README gives no other platform information
